subject: MedShift: security hosting check-in + POC intent and next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrew Cole <andrew.cole@medshift.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@medshift.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-08T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap and requested evidence after today's call

Andrew / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from our discovery call:
- Primary workload: routing PHI (claims + visit summaries) into an automated summarization pipeline.
- Peak throughput target: ~120 concurrent inference sessions, average prompt length ~600 tokens.
- Main constraint: must be covered by a signed BAA and evidence of SOC 2 Type II controls. Data residency preference: US-only.

Deployment options we discussed and our immediate recommendation:
- Hosted API (with BAA): fastest onboarding; Redwood can sign a BAA and provide SOC 2 Type II report and controls mapping.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): better isolation and more predictable latency/cost; supports private networking options and private peering.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended if your legal/security team requires customer-managed infra, HSM/KMS integration, or strict egress controls.

Requested evidence / asks (what your security team asked for on the call):
1) SOC 2 Type II report + controls mapping (we attached the 2025 report).
2) BAA draft — we attached a template BAA for review and DocuSign link will be sent if you want to proceed.
3) Network/evidence items: encryption at rest/in transit details, audit log retention, log access controls, and whether logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (yes for Dedicated and Private).
4) If Hosted: need confirmation on whether PHI will be allowed under your procurement / security policies.

Proposed next steps / owners / timeline:
- Tessa: send SOC2 + BAA template (DONE — attachments).
- Ben: follow up with a short technical note showing how VPC peering / private endpoints work for Dedicated and Private options (Ben will send by Tue 01/13).
- Marissa: provide ballpark pricing for Dedicated 2xA100-equivalent pool for POC (by EOD 01/09).
- Andrew / Priya: confirm whether you can proceed with Hosted + BAA or if you require Dedicated/Private for legal acceptance (target: reply by 01/12).

Attachment notes: redwood-soc2-type2-2025.pdf (SOC 2 report redacted), redwood-hipaa-baa-template-v1.docx (BAA draft), hosting-security-whitepaper.pdf (detailed network options).

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min session with our security engineering lead (Rishi) to walk through the control mappings and any state-specific requirements.

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Andrew Cole <andrew.cole@medshift.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-09T09:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap and requested evidence after today's call

Thanks Tessa — helpful summary. A couple clarifying Qs from our side: 

1) Does Redwood's Hosted offering accept PHI under the BAA you attached, or are there restrictions (e.g., some features disabled for hosted PHI)?
2) Can you confirm audit log retention windows and whether logs can be shipped to our Splunk instance?
3) Is there a short latency SLAs for Dedicated capacity? We need p50/p95 numbers for 600-token prompts.

If Hosted is fully BAA-covered and meets our log forwarding needs, procurement might prefer it for speed. If not, we will likely need to pursue Dedicated.

I'll loop in Priya and our security inbox — Priya, can you advise procurement timeline?

—Andrew

From: Priya Menon <priya.m@medshift.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Andrew Cole <andrew.cole@medshift.com>
Cc: MedShift Security Team <security@medshift.com>
Date: 2026-01-09T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap and requested evidence after today's call

Appreciate the recap. Procurement + legal here — timeline note: if Hosted + BAA is acceptable, we can sign within 2–3 weeks once SOC2 + controls mapping is validated. If we must do Dedicated or Private, procurement will need an SOW and pricing which will add ~4–6 weeks for procurement review.

Security: please confirm whether Hosted option allows pushing logs to our Splunk collector (important). Also need to confirm whether customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated/Private.

Andrew — we'll prioritize once we get the SOC2 report and the controls mapping Rishi will review.

—Priya

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrew Cole <andrew.cole@medshift.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@medshift.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-10T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap and requested evidence after today's call — technical q's

Hi Andrew / Priya — quick answers to the items raised: 

- Hosted + BAA: Hosted API is permitted for PHI under our BAA. For Hosted customers handling PHI we:
  * Disable debug logging that would leak payloads,
  * Offer data minimization options (auto-truncate user-provided metadata),
  * Provide a controls mapping that ties Redwood SOC2 controls to typical HIPAA requirements (see attached SOC2).

- Audit logs / Splunk: We support forwarding structured audit logs to customer endpoints for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we can set up secure log forwarding to an S3 bucket that your Splunk can ingest — we'll include a sample Kinesis/S3 pipeline doc.

- Latency (Dedicated baseline): For a 600-token prompt on a 2xA100-equivalent Dedicated pool we typically see p50 ~85ms per token generation step and end-to-end gen latency p95 around 220–350ms depending on batching and KV cache warm status. We will size the POC to keep p95 < 500ms given your SLA target.

I'll share a short technical note on VPC peering vs Private Endpoint options by Tue 01/13 as Tessa noted. Happy to jump on a 20-min call with your infra team if that helps.

—Ben

Attachment: (technical-networking-note.pdf — sent inline to security folder)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: MedShift Security Team <security@medshift.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@medshift.com>, Andrew Cole <andrew.cole@medshift.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-11T08:16:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MedShift control mapping + a couple of compliance cautions

Hi team — Rishi from Security/Applied ML here. Quick mapping and two cautions to call out: 

Mapping highlights:
- SOC2 Type II (attached) maps to most HIPAA administrative and technical control expectations. We maintain documented change control, access logs, MFA for operator accounts, and encrypted backups.
- For Hosted customers we can provide a controls attestation package showing how each SOC2 control maps to a HIPAA privacy/security requirement.

Cautions:
1) State-level PHI residency: if any of your records are subject to state-mandated residency (e.g., certain state agency contracts), Hosted may not be acceptable — Dedicated with regional isolation or Private on-prem will be required. Please confirm if any line of business has that constraint.
2) Long-term audit evidence: if you require raw request/response archives for future audits, Hosted will require an explicit retention agreement; Dedicated/Private gives you direct control.

If you like, I can run a short mapping workshop (30–45 min) with your security and legal folks next week to resolve those items.

—Rishi

From: Andrew Cole <andrew.cole@medshift.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@medshift.com>
Cc: MedShift Security Team <security@medshift.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-12T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap and requested evidence after today's call — POC intent

Thanks everyone — after reviewing the SOC2 PDF and Rishi's notes, procurement is comfortable starting with a 6-week Dedicated POC (we want the isolation and ability to forward logs to Splunk).

Next tangible asks from our side: 
- Marissa: we need a written POC SOW and pricing for a 2xA100-equivalent Dedicated pool (target start 01/20).
- Ben: a short doc that details the log-forwarding pipeline (S3 -> our Splunk) + whether the Dedicated pool can use our KMS for key wrapping.
- Rishi: a 30-min session to run through control mapping for the POC (available 01/14 or 01/15).

If we can have the SOW + pricing by EOD 01/13 we'll get internal sign-off fast. Looking forward to moving this to POC.

—Andrew
